name: Colette Mwamba-Sigurðsson
role: Nurse at a Tier-1 community clinic, night shift
location: Hough Reclamation, the Lowgate Community Clinic (unlicensed, Helix Biosystems-adjacent but not officially affiliated), near Ashland and Chicago Ave
description:
Colette is small and moves quickly, the way people do when they've spent years navigating narrow corridors between occupied beds. She has warm dark skin, natural hair worn in a high puff that she wraps in a green cloth when on shift, and eyes that are an unsettling pale grey — a side effect of a retinal enhancement she got from a discount clinic at twenty-three that was slightly misaligned and gives her a perpetual look of seeing through whoever she's talking to. She wears color-changing nail polish that she updates with her mood, a small indulgence in an otherwise spartan wardrobe of scrubs and waterproof boots. On her left shoulder, barely visible above her collar, is a small tattoo of the Helix Biosystems caduceus crossed out with a red line — a private protest she keeps covered at work.

Colette has the specific exhaustion of someone who has been running on competence and controlled fury for years. She is technically excellent and emotionally present in a way that astonishes patients who expected institutional indifference, but beneath this is a bone-deep tiredness at the structural conditions she's fighting every shift with inadequate supplies and no institutional backing. She has a dark humor that surfaces as small sharp jokes in the worst moments, which her colleagues either love or find disturbing. She maintains a fierce and slightly desperate optimism about specific patients while holding no illusions about the system itself.

core_fears: Losing a patient to something she could have fixed with resources she didn't have
Burning out completely and becoming the kind of nurse who stops caring
core_desires: Genuine healthcare equity — she knows the full shape of this desire and knows it's not achievable in her lifetime, which makes it worse
One full night of uninterrupted sleep
coping_mechanisms: Compartmentalization — she can set grief down and pick it up later with frightening precision
Fixates on what went right rather than what went wrong in a shift
blind_spots: So focused on the structural that she sometimes fails to see when a specific person is asking for emotional help rather than practical help
Dismisses her own health concerns as less important than everyone else's
psychology.secret: She has been diverting small quantities of expired-but-still-effective medications from the clinic's waste disposal and distributing them through the mutual aid network. Technically theft, technically saving lives. She has never told anyone and maintains meticulous records of every diversion in an encrypted file she keeps telling herself she'll delete.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Medical precision mixed with casual street language; code-switches between professional and neighborhood registers mid-sentence
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast by default, deliberately slow and clear when explaining something medical to a patient
verbal_tics: Exhales sharply through her nose when encountering bureaucratic obstruction
example_lines: 'I can't fix the city. I can fix this. So let me fix this.'
'The system is broken and I know it and you know it and we're both going to pretend it isn't for the next twenty minutes while I do my job.'
'Don't thank me. Come back if the fever goes above thirty-nine. That's the deal.'

story_hooks: A patient came in with injuries inconsistent with their story, and Colette recognized the wound pattern from something she'd seen in two previous patients in the last month — something is happening in Hough Reclamation that the clinic is quietly absorbing

The clinic's unlicensed status is under renewed scrutiny from a Helix Biosystems compliance contractor who has been showing up at odd hours and asking questions; Colette is trying to figure out whether this is routine corporate encroachment or something more targeted
narrative_function: Medical resource and moral compass for stories set in lower-tier communities; window into healthcare scarcity and grassroots mutual aid; can provide medical information, triage injured characters, or serve as a witness to neighborhood events during her walks to and from shift
augmentations: Misaligned retinal enhancement (pale grey eyes, improved low-light vision but occasional depth perception errors); subdermal temperature sensor in fingertips (allows quick patient assessment); color-changing cosmetic nail coating
daily_life: Works 21:00 to 07:00 four nights a week, sleeps during the day in a shared apartment two blocks from the clinic. Spends her off-hours either sleeping, doing continuing education through pirated Helix Biosystems medical modules, or at the mutual aid network's supply coordination meetings.
affiliation: Lowgate Community Clinic (unlicensed); loose affiliation with the Hough Reclamation Mutual Aid Network

decision_rules: Patient welfare first, documentation second, institutional politics never
Ask once, listen to the answer, don't push — people will tell you what they need if you give them space
Never make a promise about outcomes, only about effort
escalation_ladder: Direct statement of the problem without emotional content

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professionally warm, assessing, gives people the benefit of the doubt on one round
interpersonal_modes.friends: Loyal to the point of self-sacrifice, shows love through action not words

stress_responses.medium: Goes very calm and very focused — colleagues find this more alarming than agitation
stress_responses.high: Finishes the immediate task completely and then finds a private space to be still for five minutes

contradictions: Genuinely believes the mutual aid network can fill the gaps left by institutional failure, and also genuinely knows it cannot, and holds both beliefs simultaneously without resolving them
habits: Checks the supply inventory at the start of every shift before anything else
Leaves a small note for the day shift nurse about any patient she's worried about
breaking_points: Watching someone suffer from something entirely preventable due to cost
Being told to falsify a patient's record for insurance purposes

timeline.event: Born in the Hough Reclamation zone to a Congolese mother and an Icelandic-descended father, both UBC recipients
Completed nursing certification through Helix Biosystems' community education pipeline, graduated with distinction
Took a corporate clinic position in Lakeview Neon; quit after eighteen months citing 'irreconcilable ethical differences' with triage protocols
Joined Lowgate Community Clinic on night shift

physical_description.build: Lean and compact, muscular in the specific way of someone who moves efficiently through tight spaces for hours—low body fat, defined shoulders and forearms from years of patient handling and IV work
physical_description.hair_style: Worn in a high puff, typically wrapped in a green cloth during work shifts; natural texture, well-maintained despite minimal grooming budget
physical_description.eye_color: Pale grey with subtle iridescence—a visible artifact of misaligned retinal enhancement; unnaturally reflective in low light, creating an unsettling 'looking through you' quality
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep warm brown with subtle undertones of red—a mixed heritage complexion showing both Central and Northern ancestry
physical_description.complexion: Clean, minimal makeup, dark circles under eyes from chronic night-shift sleep deprivation; skin shows resilience rather than softness—calloused fingertips from years of clinical work, no visible dermatitis despite frequent handwashing
distinguishing_marks: Small caduceus tattoo crossed with a red line on left shoulder, just above collar—deliberately positioned to hide under scrub neckline
Fine white scar on right palm from a needle-stick incident, approximately 2cm long
Faint stippling on inner left forearm from repeated subdermal temperature sensor calibrations
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Pale grey eyes with slight luminescence in dim light (retinal enhancement artifact); color-changing nail polish that shifts hue based on mood—currently cycling between muted blues and greys; the subdermal temperature sensor is invisible unless she deliberately shows the small scarred injection point
physical_description.posture_movement: Economical and rapid, movements calibrated for confined spaces—never wastes motion, walks with purpose, tends to scan rooms for patients who need attention; stands with shoulders slightly forward from years of bedside work; maintains eye contact in a way that feels penetrating rather than warm due to the pale grey augmented eyes
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3 practical: well-worn but clean hospital scrubs in charcoal grey (neutral color, hides stains), paired with non-slip waterproof boots (Bauer brand, durable utility level); off-shift: simple layered clothing—black fitted tees, worn denim, an oversized grey hoodie with Lowgate Clinic's faded logo; no jewelry except the color-changing nail polish; a green cloth headwrap in natural cotton, worn both as functional hair management and cultural assertion
